title: Pad suppression + kernel-sway labnotes
content:
Purpose: running exploratory profiling to understand how pad suppression (skipping work for padded tokens) interacts with kernel selection heuristics (FlashAttention vs paged attention vs fused ops). Goal is actionable tuning guidance for the scheduler: when to prefer fused kernels, when to route to paged, and when pad-heavy batches should use a different prefetch strategy.

Background/context:
- We recently added pad-aware batching at the request path (RINF-8421). Basic idea: avoid computing attention for padding tokens by adjusting sequence offsets and masking, and in many cases avoid copying padded KV chunks into GPU memory.
- Serving runtime currently chooses kernels based primarily on sequence length and batch size heuristics (seq_len * batch_size thresholds). Fusion-enabled builds prefer fused matmul+softmax kernels when no masking/reguations appear.
- Empirical issue: enabling pad suppression reduces total FLOPs for the logical workload but seems to push some batches into kernels with worse latency variance and increased kernel handoffs. Observed bursts and p95 spikes.

Hardware / software baseline used in experiments:
- HW: AWS p4d (8xA100-40GB), single-worker experiments used 1 GPU.
- Driver/CUDA: 11.8; cuBLAS/cuDNN: vendor defaults; nvprof/Nsight sampling for traces.
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (commit 2f7a3c) + local patch to instrument kernel handoffs (PR linked).
- FlashAttention: v2 (patched for streaming); Paged attention: runtime implementation with explicit page prefetch and KV packing.
- Models: llama-2-7b, gptj-6b-small eval snippet (to vary head dims).
- Workload mixes: synthetic (fixed seq lengths: 16/64/512 mix), and production-sampled (real request traces from last 24h obfuscated).

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Variables:
  - pad_ratio: low (<10%), medium (10-40%), high (>40%) measured as (total padded tokens)/(total tokens) in a batch.
  - seq_mix: narrow (all same len) vs skewed (50% short, 50% long) vs uniform.
  - batch_size (effective): 1, 4, 8 (small-batch regime where kernel choice matters).
  - fusion_flag: on/off; fused kernel allowed only when mask complexity <= threshold.
  - prefetch_mode: eager vs gated (prefetch only when pad_ratio < t).

Key measurements collected per test run:
- end-to-end p50/p95/p99 token latency (ms)
- kernel_handoff_count (how many times runtime switched kernel strategy mid-request)
- handoff_latency_ms (time spent in kernel scheduling handoff)
- GPU utilization (SM%, memory BW)
- kernel occupancy / register spills (approximated via Nsight counters)
- memcpy count / memcopy bytes for KV copies
- fusion_failure_rate (fused kernel returned non-ok or fell back)

Representative command used (local harness):
./run_micro_workload --model llama-2-7b --batch 4 --seqmix skewed --pad-suppression on --fusion on --trace kernel,mem --out /tmp/run1

Observations (summary):
1) Small-batch + high pad_ratio -> increased handoffs and worse p95
   - When pad_ratio > ~45% in batch with small effective batch sizes (<=4), runtime frequently flips between fused and paged kernels. Why: fused kernel sees irregular warp execution because the mask branches are sparse, causing divergence and register pressure. The kernel's internal heuristics then time out and the runtime schedules a fallback paged kernel which has higher per-op overhead. The extra handoff cost and cache churn yields p95 spikes.

2) Pad suppression reduces memcpy bytes but increases kernel occupancy variance
   - We saved ~25-40% of KV memcpy depending on the workload. However, reduced contiguousness of the KV layout (we pack sequences tightly) increases address irregularity and caused increased memory transaction inefficiency in some kernels (FlashAttention expects contiguous blocks for optimal coalescing).

3) Fusion-sensitive tipping point correlates with pad_entropy, not just pad_ratio
   - pad_entropy (how uneven padding is across batch elements) matters. A batch where 40% of tokens are pad but concentrated in only 1 element is better for fusion than the same pad_ratio spread evenly across all elements. Fusion prefers localized padding (makes masking cheap) vs dispersed padding (causes divergence).

4) Paged attention's prefetch policy is sensitive to page-fragmentation after packing
   - Our paged prefetcher sees more small page requests (increased page fragmentation), driving more PCIe/GPU DMA ops. Eager prefetching became net-worse for pad-heavy mixes; gated prefetch (skip prefetch if pad_ratio > 30%) reduced memcopy overhead and improved p50 by ~8% for those cases.

5) Fused ops show lower median but heavier tail when mask complexity high
   - For low-mask-complexity cases fused ops are best: p50 ~20% lower than paged. For high dispersion masks, fused ops had micro-stalls causing sporadic spills -> p99 increases.

Instrumented metrics to add to runtime (proposal):
- kernel_handoff_count (existing) -> enrich with handoff_cause tag (pad_entropy / seq_variance / mem_pressure)
- pad_ratio, pad_entropy emitted as trace fields per request
- fused_kernel_backoff_counter (how many times we disabled fusion due to spills)
- prefetch_skipped_due_to_pad (count)

Scheduler / heuristic changes proposed:
1) Use a 2D decision surface: (effective_batch_size, pad_entropy) instead of scalar seq_len threshold. Rationale: batch size scales compute parallelism, pad_entropy predicts divergence risk.
2) Add a small hysteresis window to kernel choice to avoid frequent switching: require N requests or T ms of improved latency before switching back to previous kernel. (Mitigates handoff thrash for mixed traffic.)
3) Prefetch gating: if pad_ratio > 30% or pad_entropy > 0.6, disable eager prefetch and use on-demand page fetch with coalescing.
4) Add a micro-benchmark at warmup that measures fused-kernel register pressure for current model dims and uses that to set an occupancy threshold. (Avoid relying purely on empirical global numbers.)

Micro-experiment: handoff cost quantification
- Method: craft request stream that toggles between high-pad and low-pad every 10s and measure latency delta and number of handoffs.
- Result: average handoff_latency_ms = 12.2ms (std 3.8). Handoff has non-negligible cost in small-batch workloads and appears to correlate with p95.

Open anomalies / follow-ups:
- Strange NVTX grouping: some fused kernels report >2x register usage in Nsight but execution time doesn't match. Hypothesis: sampling artifact from async memory ops. Need raw CUPTI trace.
- For GPTJ-like heads, fusion is less stable because head-shape (head dim) interacts with tiling in fused kernel; test more head dims.
- Paged prefetcher sometimes prefetches pages that are then evicted by the next request (thrash) when padding causes packing to shift memory layout. Consider LRU boosting for recently-prefetched pages per worker.

Action items (short):
- [Asha] wire pad_entropy and pad_ratio into request trace (RINF-8490) - done locally, push small PR for structured traces (linked).
- [Marco] implement hysteresis guard in kernel-choice (proto branch: kernel-hysteresis) and run A/B against production-sampled traces.
- [Priya] add fused_kernel_backoff_counter metric in runtime and hook to Console dashboards (create ticket for dashboard).
- [Ethan] collect CUPTI traces for anomalous fused kernel samples (open timeslots next Tue).

Notes to self / rough checklist for follow-up experiments:
- test with A100-80GB and H100 to check register pressure differences
- add synthetic skewed entropy generator to reproduce pad dispersion cases reliably
- test gated prefetch threshold sweep (10% increments) and measure end-to-end cost/latency tradeoff
- instrument memory fragmentation metric (pages_per_batch, avg_page_fill)

Concluding thought:
Pad suppression is great for reducing raw compute and memcpy, but it changes memory layout and mask dispersion in ways that expose weaknesses in fusion heuristics. Instead of turning fusion off globally, we should make kernel selection pad-aware (both ratio + entropy) and add small stability mechanisms (hysteresis + micro-bench warmup) to avoid oscillation. The result should keep median latency benefits of fusion while reducing p95/p99 spikes for production mixes.
